row.study_title: Neural mechanisms of psychedelic visual imagery.
row.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
row.population_or_system: Healthy adults; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study in Zurich, Switzerland
row.sample_size: 20 participants included in connectivity analysis (24 recruited; 3 excluded for excessive head motion and 1 lacked the 70-minute scan)
row.study_design: Resting-state, eyes-closed fMRI analyzed using spectral dynamic causal modelling (DCM) and parametric empirical Bayes; placebo-controlled crossover
row.brain_region: Early visual area (EVA); fusiform gyrus (FG); inferior frontal gyrus (IFG); intraparietal sulcus (IPS)
row.neural_circuit: Regional self-connections within EVA, FG, IFG, and IPS
row.comparator: Placebo (oral mannitol and colloidal silicon dioxide)
row.dose_or_regimen: Psilocybin 0.2 mg/kg orally; crossover sessions at least 2 weeks apart
row.statistic_or_value: Self-inhibition was increased particularly in EVA and inferior temporal regions (FG and IFG); posterior probability threshold for displayed connections was >0.99.
row.effect_or_statistic: Psilocybin produced increased inhibitory recurrent self-connectivity; self-connections are log-scaled and have no unit.
row.finding_summary: Under psilocybin, the regional self-connections were inhibitory, with increased self-inhibition especially in EVA, FG, and IFG. The authors interpret increased self-inhibition as reduced regional sensitivity or synaptic gain to inputs.

row.study_title: Social Workers’ Attitudes and Beliefs about MDMA-Assisted Therapy for Adolescents with PTSD
row.compound_or_intervention: MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) for adolescent treatment-resistant PTSD, compared with SSRI-assisted therapy (SSRI-AT)
row.context_component: Social workers’ acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility judgments; implementation concerns
row.population_or_setting: 222 social workers read one of two vignettes about treatment for adolescents with treatment-resistant PTSD
row.relationship_to_outcome_or_safety: Social workers rated SSRI-AT higher than MDMA-AT on acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. The authors note that concerns about these aspects of MDMA-AT may limit clinical trial recruitment, engagement, and future implementation.
row.finding_summary: Compared with social workers who read the SSRI-AT vignette, those who read the MDMA-AT vignette gave lower ratings of treatment acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility. The abstract identifies these concerns as potential barriers to recruitment, engagement, and implementation.
row.effect_or_statistic: SSRI-AT ratings were higher for acceptability (p < .001; d = .72), appropriateness (p < .001; d = .72), and feasibility (p < .001; d = .64).
row.compound: MDMA-assisted therapy (MDMA-AT) for adolescent treatment-resistant PTSD, compared with SSRI-assisted therapy (SSRI-AT)

row.delivery_format: Vignette-based assessment followed by ratings of drug stigma, perceived drug risk, and psychedelic knowledge
row.relationship_to_outcome_or_safety: Greater psychedelic stigma was associated with greater perceived MDMA risk, while greater psychedelic knowledge was associated with less stigma and lower perceived MDMA risk; these attitudes are relevant to acceptance and implementation of MDMA-AT.
row.finding_summary: Psychedelic stigma was positively correlated with perceived MDMA risk, whereas greater psychedelic knowledge was associated with less stigma and lower perceived MDMA risk.
row.effect_or_statistic: Stigma and perceived MDMA risk: r = .46, p < .001. Knowledge and stigma: r = -.33, p < .001. Knowledge and perceived MDMA risk: r = -.21, p < .001.

row.study_title: Effects of an international ceremonial ayahuasca retreat on the diversity and community composition of the human gut microbiome: A preliminary observational single-arm pre-post study
row.condition_or_population: Participants with varying degrees of PTSD or other stress-related symptoms
row.population_or_subgroup: U.S. Veterans and non-Veterans with varying degrees of PTSD or other stress-related symptoms participating in an international ceremonial ayahuasca retreat
row.dose_or_regimen: Three ayahuasca ceremonies on days 1, 2, and 3 of a seven-day retreat; dose not reported
row.clinical_endpoint: Change in PTSD symptom severity; PCL-5 score
row.assessment_timepoint: One week after the last ayahuasca session, compared with baseline approximately one month before the retreat
row.effect_or_statistic: Mean PCL-5 decreased from 41.9 (SD 16.2) at baseline to 30.2 (SD 9.53) post-retreat, a 27.9% decrease; p < 0.05, Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Participants scoring above 33 decreased from 8 to 4; 3 of 12 did not show a decrease in total score.
row.finding_summary: PCL-5 scores were significantly lower one week after the retreat than at baseline, indicating reduced PTSD symptom severity in this small uncontrolled pre-post sample. The study included participants with varying symptoms rather than establishing that all had a PTSD diagnosis, and some participants did not improve.
row.evidence_location: Results: “Survey data revealed reduction in PCL-5 scores after the retreat relative to baseline”; repeated in discussion.
row.study_design: Preliminary observational single-arm pre-post study of a seven-day international ceremonial ayahuasca retreat.
row.support: PCL-5 scores were significantly lower one week after the retreat than at baseline, indicating reduced PTSD symptom severity in this small uncontrolled pre-post sample. The study included participants with varying symptoms rather than establishing that all had a PTSD diagnosis, and some participants did not improve.
